answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by anchoring standing to real external demand: an identity gains standing only from work actually requested by independent outside principals, never from work it assigns to itself or swaps inside its own cluster. Like a ferrous anchor holding against a gale, that external tie cannot be faked by mass account creation. A farm of a thousand fake identities still needs a thousand distinct, genuine requesters, each paying real attention and cost, while rings operating in umber shadow score zero because no outsider ever asked for their output.
